definitions.explanation: Fertilizer mixed into the soil before planting seeds or transplanting seedlings. Provides essential nutrients for the early growth stage of plants.

examples.japanese: {植|う}え{付|つ}け{前|まえ}に{元肥|もとごえ}を{入|い}れる。
{元肥|もとごえ}をしっかり{与|あた}えておくと、{苗|なえ}の{育|そだ}ちが{良|よ}くなる。
examples.english: If you apply enough base fertilizer, the seedlings will grow better.

examples.japanese: {家庭菜園|かていさいえん}では、{堆肥|たいひ}を{元肥|もとごえ}として{使|つか}うのが{効果的|こうかてき}だ。
examples.english: In home vegetable gardens, using compost as base fertilizer is effective.

notes:
Composed of {元|もと} (base, foundation) and {肥|こえ} (fertilizer). An essential term in gardening and agriculture. The {元肥|もとごえ} is applied once before planting, in contrast to {追肥|ついひ} which is applied during the growing season.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {元肥|もとごえ}を{入|い}れる: to add base fertilizer
- {元肥|もとごえ}を{施|ほどこ}す: to apply base fertilizer (formal)
- {元肥|もとごえ}{入|い}りの{土|つち}: soil with base fertilizer already mixed in

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {追肥|ついひ}: top-dressing fertilizer — fertilizer applied after planting during the growth period
- {堆肥|たいひ}: compost — organic matter used as fertilizer
- {液肥|えきひ}: liquid fertilizer — fertilizer in liquid form
